t: You are on Moorgate, once one of the northern gates in the City of London's defensive wall, and the last to be built. It took its name from Moorfields, the marshy land that lay just north of the wall. The poet John Keats was born here. He died of tuberculosis at just 25, with his poems in print for less than four years. They were indifferently received in his lifetime, but his fame grew rapidly after his death, and he is now a firm part of the canon of English literature.
